title: Tidy the Folder Path
statement: A file manager shows paths like `/school/./notes//../photos/`. Tidy the path: parts are separated by one or more `/`; a part `.` means stay in the same folder; `..` means go up one folder (and does nothing at the top folder `/`); any other part is a folder name. Return the tidy path: it starts with `/`, has single `/` between folder names, and no `/` at the end (the top folder alone is `/`).
constraints: Folder names use letters, digits, '_' and '.'; a name like '...' is a normal folder

answerKey.pattern: Split into parts, keep a stack of folder names
keyPoints: Split on '/' and skip empty parts and '.'
'..' pops the last folder if there is one
Any other part is pushed as a folder name
Join the stack with '/' and put '/' in front
edgeCases: Names like '...' that are not special
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Repeated string replacements of '/./' and '/name/../': O(n^2) and easy to get wrong

hints: The most recently entered folder is the one to leave: keep folder names on a stack.
Split the path on '/', skip '' and '.', pop on '..', push anything else, then join.
